Demolition With a Paper Trail, Not Just a Dumpster Run

c: Markham families tend to ask more questions than most about where a demolished structure actually ends up, and that’s a reasonable thing to want answered. Around Unionville and Markham Village’s heritage streets, it’s a shed or fence tucked behind a home held for decades, torn down with the same patience given to anything else on an older property. In Berczy, Cornell and the newer east-end communities, it’s structures cleared from full, often multigenerational households — a backyard several generations actually use, demolished around a busy family’s schedule rather than whenever suits us. And across the city more broadly, it’s the metal from a pool frame, a swing set or a fence line routed to certified recyclers as a matter of course, not an afterthought tacked on because someone asked. The 700+ five-star reviews behind Live Junk Free consistently mention the same detail: not just that the structure came down, but that the crew could actually say where the pieces went.

blocks.text: DEMOLITION FAQ
Demolition Services in Markham — Scoped Questions, Committed Answers

items.q: How much does demolition cost in Markham?
a: It depends on the structure — a fence section is inexpensive, a full above ground pool or a concrete patio costs more given the crew time involved. The figure is confirmed free at the walkthrough and includes certified recycling for metal components.

items.q: Where does the metal from a demolished pool or fence actually go?
a: To certified recyclers, not a generic dump run. Documentation of what was recycled is available if your household wants the record.

items.q: Can demolition work around a busy multigenerational household?
a: Yes — it’s common work for us in Berczy and Cornell. Scheduling accounts for a household with several generations and several schedules under one roof.

items.q: How careful are you with older homes in Unionville or Markham Village?
a: Very. Original features that stay get masked and protected, and the work moves at the pace a heritage property deserves.

items.q: What's involved in concrete or flooring demolition?
a: The patio, walkway or pad gets broken up with equipment matched to its thickness, then hauled off in manageable pieces. The site is left level and cleared.
